overall: The AG found no OML violation for the privilege-based redactions to executive session minutes, but found one redaction under Purpose 1 unauthorized, and declined to review late-raised concerns.

allegations.summary: Complainants challenged Board redactions to executive session minutes about the Town Manager's contract, claiming attorney-client privilege was improperly applied.
allegations.key_passage: Because the relevant portions of the executive session minutes are no longer being withheld from the public under the Open Meeting Law, we find no violation of that law.

allegations.summary: Board redacted part of a Town Manager statement in the November 30 executive session minutes, relying on executive session Purpose 1 under the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Based on information provided by the Board, and the fact that the executive session was held pursuant to section 21(a)(2) (executive session Purpose 2) and not pursuant to Purpose 1, we find that the Open Meeting Law does not authorize this redaction.

allegations.summary: Complainants requested notes, recordings and other preparatory materials for the executive session minutes and session documents, which the Board may have withheld.
allegations.key_passage: It is our understanding that the Board does not rely on the Open Meeting Law to withhold any documents relevant to the subject matter at issue in this complaint.

allegations.summary: Later memorandum raised concerns about draft versus unredacted minutes and whether minutes were a faithful transcription, which were not in the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review these additional concerns because, to the extent they may allege violations of the Open Meeting Law, they were not raised in an original complaint filed with the Board.
